acceptance_criteria: Holm-adjusted lagged TYVIX CAR p-value below 0.05 (one-sided, negative direction)
Standardized mean lagged TYVIX CAR at or below -0.3
spec.alternative_hypothesis: The lagged TYVIX CAR[0,+1] is negative, with a Holm-adjusted one-sided p-value below 0.05 and a standardized mean CAR at or below -0.3.
spec.benchmark: Constant-mean expected return: the mean observed change over each event's own estimation window [-60,-11], estimated separately per event and per leg, on the lagged changes for the FRED legs
cost_assumptions: No cost gate applies: an event study measures announcement responses, not a forecast, and there is no trading rule to cost. A significant CAR is evidence about how markets respond to scheduled announcements, not a tradable edge.
spec.cost_model: No cost gate: an event study measures announcement responses, not a forecast; there is no trading rule to cost
exclusions: Unscheduled meetings, cancelled meetings, conference calls and notation votes are excluded (same event set as study 005).
FOMC minutes releases are not events in this study.
Events with an incomplete estimation window ([-60,-11]) or event window ([0,+1]) are excluded and counted.
The first panel return row (2003-01-03) is dropped: it has no lagged change.
Bars outside the sample (2003-01-02 to 2020-05-15) are out of sample for the main tests.
The per-day abnormal-return decomposition and the unlagged replication on the truncated index are descriptive only and are not in the test family.
fixed_parameters: event_source=federalreserve fomchistorical pages 2003-2020 and fomccalendars.htm 2021 onwards
lag_verification=2026-11-18 VIXCLS/DGS10 fredgraph CSVs fetched 06:26 UTC end 2026-11-16 (Monday); Tuesday 2026-11-17 not yet posted, Monday already available
statement_time=14:00 ET on the last meeting day
known_confounders: The lagged test answers a different question than study 005: the lagged [0,+1] window covers reference-date changes [-1,0], so a changed verdict does not mean the original conclusion was wrong; both are conditionally correct under different availability assumptions.
The FRED posting lag is verified by behaviour on 2026-11-18 only; the residual risk is a historical change in FRED's posting behaviour, which cannot be verified from current data.
The estimation window also shifts back one day in reference terms ([-61,-12]); the effect on a 50-day mean is second-order.
A partial holiday in one FRED leg is handled per series on its own dates: a lagged change at t is the original change at the previous own date, even when that date is not in the panel index.
TYVIX was discontinued in May 2020; the main sample ends 2020-05-15 and excludes the post-2020 hiking cycle.

Estimation windows may contain a prior meeting's event window (2 of 50 days when meetings are five weeks apart); the contamination is small and the simple [-60,-11] rule is kept as preregistered, mirroring study 005.
Other macro releases occasionally coincide with FOMC statement days; they are not excluded — the event window is defined by the FOMC calendar only.
The SPX control must reproduce study 005's SPX CAR (+0.000669, p=0.634) exactly; a mismatch would indicate a machinery error, not a market finding.
spec.mechanism: FRED posts a value dated t on the next business day (verified 2026-11-18: one-trading-day availability lag), so a reader or system depending on FRED's publication rhythm sees the statement-day change only at t+1. The lagged [0,+1] window therefore covers reference-date changes [-1,0]: the statement-day change plus the day-before change. If the TYVIX drop is concentrated on day 0, the lagged CAR stays negative; if it is concentrated on day +1, the lagged CAR collapses toward the day -1 noise. Study 005's conclusion is correct under reference-date alignment; this study asks what a reader or system depending on FRED's publication rhythm would conclude. Both are conditionally correct under different availability assumptions — a changed verdict here does not mean the original conclusion was wrong.
spec.missing_data_policy: No forward filling; drop incomplete synchronized rows and report the dropped count. Events whose t=0 is absent from the panel or whose estimation or event window does not fit inside the panel are excluded and counted (same event set as study 005: 135 included, 3 excluded). The first panel return row (2003-01-03) has no lagged change and is dropped.
model_definition: Constant-mean event study via the repo event_study() estimator (estimation window [-60,-11], event window [0,+1], overlap-cluster inference), mirroring study 005
FRED legs lagged one trading day on their own dates (diff-then-join, shift between diff and join); Yahoo SPX not shifted

One-sided p-values for the lagged volatility legs derived from the estimator z-statistic as Phi(z) for the 'less than' direction; two-sided p-values for lagged DGS10, lagged BAA10Y and the SPX control
Holm family of 5 tests (a lagged TYVIX, b lagged VIX, c lagged DGS10, d lagged BAA10Y, e SPX unlagged control); effect size is the standardized mean CAR
Descriptive per-day abnormal-return decomposition (day -1, 0, +1 contributions, unlagged) and descriptive unlagged replication on the truncated panel index (no p-values)
spec.multiple_testing_family: Lagged FOMC event-window CARs (5 tests: a lagged TYVIX CAR[0,+1] < 0, b lagged VIX CAR[0,+1] < 0, c lagged DGS10 CAR[0,+1] != 0, d lagged BAA10Y CAR[0,+1] != 0, e SPX CAR[0,+1] != 0 unlagged control)
spec.null_hypothesis: The lagged TYVIX CAR[0,+1] is zero: under FRED's publication rhythm the statement-day response is not visible in the [0,+1] availability window.
spec.primary_metric: Standardized mean lagged TYVIX CAR[0,+1] (mean CAR divided by the cross-event standard deviation of CARs)
rejection_criteria: Holm-adjusted lagged TYVIX CAR p-value at or above 0.05 (one-sided, negative direction)
Standardized mean lagged TYVIX CAR above -0.3
spec.research_question: Does study 005's TYVIX event response (CAR[0,+1] = -0.0381, Holm p = 5.0e-08) survive when every FRED series is shifted one trading day to match FRED's publication rhythm — that is, when the reader sees each FRED value only the next trading day?
spec.target_definition: Per-leg cumulative abnormal return over the lagged [0,+1] event window around scheduled FOMC statement days (FRED legs lagged one trading day: VIX and TYVIX log changes, DGS10 and BAA10Y level changes in basis points; SPX log return unlagged as an internal correctness control)
spec.title: The FOMC TYVIX event response survives a one-day FRED lag
